issues.message: 394 blocks, over the common budget of 350 (docs/STRUCTURES.md). A warning only.
The roof does not reach past the walls on any two opposite sides: give it one block of overhang.

notes.purpose: Without bookshelves (they come in L2) the hall reads as a plain house with a table, chairs and barrels; only the big glass front gable hints at a library.
notes.detail: Buttresses, timber posts and the front glass are good, but the stacks are empty and there are no props outside.
notes.roof: Steep 45-degree roof with one block of overhang on all four sides (eaves at x1/x9, z0/z10), dark oak eaves and ridge stripe: the automatic overhang warning is a false alarm.
notes.shape: A plain rectangle under one gable roof; the brick chimney is the only break. The great window reads as a stepped grid of panes rather than round.

visual.summary: Stone reading hall shell with a glazed front gable, buttressed walls, a reading table, hearth, archive barrels and a scribe desk at the back.
problems: L1 does not read as a library: put at least a couple of bookshelves (or a lectern) in L1 so the job shows from the first build; L2 can still fill the rest of the stacks.
Reach: the whole hall floor is reached; only roof slopes, bookshelf tops and stair tops are unreached - fine.
